architecture: replication

auth:
  enabled: true
master:
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: 2
      memory: 4Gi

  enabled: false

  enabled: false

  create: false

serviceAccount:
  create: true
  automount: false

```bash
  --values redis/redis-phoenix-values.yaml \
  --wait
```


upgrade failed

 helm upgrade --install redis-phoenix bitnami/redis -f redis/redis-phoenix-values.yaml --set global.redis.password=FDe4sXw43h
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: cannot patch "redis-phoenix-replicas" with kind StatefulSet: StatefulSet.apps "redis-phoenix-replicas" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than 'replicas', 'ordinals', 'template', 'updateStrategy', 'revisionHistoryLimit', 'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy' and 'minReadySeconds' are forbidden

The StatefulSet has immutable fields that can't be changed. You need to delete and recreate it. Here's the safest approach:

```bash
# 1. Scale down replicas to 0 first
kubectl scale statefulset redis-phoenix-replicas --replicas=0 -n default

# 2. Delete the StatefulSet (keeps the PVCs)
kubectl delete statefulset redis-phoenix-replicas -n default

# 3. Scale down master
kubectl scale statefulset redis-phoenix-master --replicas=0 -n default

# 4. Delete master StatefulSet
kubectl delete statefulset redis-phoenix-master -n default

# 5. Now upgrade (use the OCI registry like before)
helm upgrade redis-phoenix oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts/redis \
  --version 21.1.11 \
  --namespace default \
  --values redis/redis-phoenix-values.yaml \
  --set global.redis.password=FDe4sXw43h \
  --wait
```

**Note:** This will cause downtime. The PVCs (persistent volumes) will be preserved and reattached to the new pods, so your data should remain intact.
